---
title: Serialization format of tokenization without analysis
---



## Block structure

Tokenization of a passage and segmentation into sentences can be serialized without incurring the cost of a full syntactic anlaysis. The results are serialized to a plain-text format with delimited-text data blocks labelled `#!sentences`, and `#!tokens`.  By default, the pipe character `|` is used as a delimiter in delimited-text blocks.


## Field structure

The structure of each block type is illustrated with the serialization of an analysis of a passage with text content `arma virumque cano` and CTS URN `urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1`.


### Sentences

`#!sentences` blocks have four columns with a header `context_begin|first_token|context_end|last_token`. These give the URN content and token ID of the first and last tokens of each sentence. (This is identical to the `#!sentences` block [serialized for a full analysis](./analysisformat.qmd).)


**Example**:

```
#!sentences
context_begin|first_token|context_end|last_token
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1|t0|urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003.omar:1.1|t3
```


### Tokens

The  `#!tokens` block has four columns with the header `context|sentence_index|id|text`. These give the CTS URN, a sentence index number, and the token ID for each token, followed by the text content of the token.


```
#!tokens
context|sentence_index|id|text
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003:1.1|0|t0|arma
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003:1.1|0|t1|virum
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003:1.1|0|t2|que
urn:cts:latinLit:phi0690.phi003:1.1|0|t3|cano
```
